craft_notes: Sthāyin: the seal (paper-thin finale: quivering pith, ever near, I hymn). Rows: row 3 (at-hand→hymn). Close: hymn (naumi — first and only hymn-verb; praise/bow/honor yield to hymning at the seal). Rejected: 'circle of gods' — killed: god-ring kept (cakra as ring, tighter); ending on doctrine — killed: I-hymn kept (the tantra ends on the singer).

lines: Quivering pith of experience, in all ends, ever at hand:
thus ever risen, my body's god-ring — I hymn.
l4.sanskrit_cite: saṃsphuradanubhavasāraṃ sarvāntaḥ satatasannihitam | naumi sadoditamitthaṃ nijadehagadevatācakram

reads_against.argmap: How does it close? → Collective bow to the ever-present vibrating circle as first-person experience-essence; the stotra's seal.
c1_essence: The quivering experience-pith ever near: one's own god-circle hymned as first-person presence.
reads_against.c1_rasa: adbhuta settling toward śānta (wonder circling home to rest)
